February 23, 2023

RE: Seward Highway and Alyeska Highway Intersection Improvements Recommended
Alternative “Trumpet” Interchange

By request of the Girdwood Board of Supervisors (GBOS) in 2018, the Alaska Department of
Transportation studied and presented options for improving the interchange between Seward
and Alyeska Highways to improve traffic flow, safety, and access to Old Girdwood. The
community appreciates the improved road and pedestrian bridges over the railroad tracks in the
resultant plan, as well as the creation of connectivity to the Lower Iditarod Trail. Girdwood also
appreciates the meetings and open communication with R&M Consultants, Christina Huber, and
other DOT personnel.

However, the public and GBOS have several concerns related to the current recommended
design, and are opposed to the overall scope and environmental impact of the project as
proposed. As noted during the January 9th, 2023 Planning and Zoning Commission meeting,
there is a need for additional process and information for Girdwood to ensure that the ultimate
decision is a democratic collaboration between the community and DOT&PF. According to the
commission, there is a need for “a more detailed or an annotated alternatives evaluation matrix
providing information about the environmental impacts, safety, cost, and access”.
In light of those needs, the substantial cost of the project, and also the consistent community
opposition to the current project design, GBOS requests that an independent 3rd party
evaluation of the Alyeska Highway Interchange selection be commissioned by DOT, and then
shared with the community and GBOS.

We appreciate your consideration,





Jennifer Wingard
GBOS Roads & Utilities Supervisor
